result:
Review scope note: the target `main` vs. this branch differs only by two docs commits (`README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`); the working tree is clean. I therefore reviewed both those docs commits and the newest code commit on `main` (`d86d2dc`, "+ Factor" button, `app/components/panels/CausalGraphPanel.tsx`). No `ReportFindings` tool was available in this session, so the findings are listed below.

Findings

1. `/repo/app/components/panels/CausalGraphPanel.tsx:118` — **Medium.** `handleAddVariable` serializes `displayGraph`, which is `causalGraph ?? streamingPreview` (`mergeStreamingPreview`, prefers final data). During generation `app/page.tsx:428` clears the persisted string so the preview shows; if the user clicks "+ Factor" while the graph is still streaming, `onContentChange` (= `setPersistedCausalGraph`) writes the partial snapshot back, which has three consequences: (a) `causalGraph` becomes non-null, so `mergeStreamingPreview` now prefers it and the live preview visibly freezes for the rest of the stream; (b) when generation finishes, `storeArtifactResults` (`app/page.tsx:265-270`) overwrites the persisted string with the model output, silently discarding the factor the user just added; (c) if generation fails or is aborted, the persisted snapshot is partial-JSON and may lack `edges`/`confounders`, and `DetailsView` reads `causalGraph.edges.length` / `causalGraph.confounders.length` unguarded (same file, lines 69 and 87), so switching to the Details tab throws a TypeError and blanks the panel (the graph view is defensive via `useCausalGraphLayout`, Details is not). Gating the button on final data (`causalGraph`) or on `!loading` fixes all three.

2. `/repo/README.md:120` — **Low.** The "Analytics history … does not persist across Vercel function invocations" bullet understates the failure. `app/lib/analytics/persist.ts` writes to `join(process.cwd(), "data")`, which is read-only on Vercel. Writes from LLM calls are swallowed (`recordAndCache` try/catch), but `DELETE /api/analytics` (`app/api/analytics/route.ts`) calls `clearAnalyticsEntries()` → `mkdirSync` with no error handling, so clicking "Clear" in the analytics panel on a Vercel deployment returns a 500 EROFS rather than a no-op.

3. `/repo/README.md:117` — **Low.** The "Limitations on Vercel" list omits function timeouts. No API route sets `export const maxDuration`, and there is no `vercel.json`; the streaming artifact/decomposition routes (Claude Opus over full source documents) can easily exceed Vercel's default function duration, so a one-click-deployed instance will truncate long generations mid-stream. Worth either documenting or adding `maxDuration` to the streaming routes now that the README actively promotes the deploy button.

4. `/repo/README.md:53` — **Low.** The local "Install and run" section still says only `npm install && npm run dev`; the new env-var documentation lives only under "Deploy to Vercel". A local user following the README gets no key configured, and `callLlm` silently falls back to canned mock artifacts (`app/lib/llm/callLlm.ts:203`) with only a server-side console warning, so the app looks functional but is fabricating output. A one-line `.env.local` instruction in the local setup section would close this.

Checked and found correct: the mock-verifier claims in both files match `app/api/verification/lean/route.ts` (mock on any fetch/JSON failure, including the 35s timeout) and `useFormalizationPipeline` (treats `valid: true` from the mock as verified); the OpenRouter-fallback description matches `callLlm`'s Anthropic → OpenRouter → mock ordering; the deploy button's `repository-url` matches the repo used in `CONTRIBUTING.md`; and the `#deploy-to-vercel` / `#lean-verification-service` anchors both resolve.
